checks.A_encoder_gradient_flows_query_and_candi: PASSED -- encoder receives a nonzero gradient from both the pairwise (gathered positive/hard-negative candidates) and dense SmoothL1 (full-candidate-chunk) branches; neither branch silently detaches the candidate side.
checks.B_frozen_encoder_regression_receives_no_: PASSED -- with requires_grad=False on the encoder (the C0/R2 configuration), encoder_unfreeze_step accumulates exactly no gradient on any encoder parameter.
checks.C_no_stale_candidate_bank_embeddings_tra: PASSED -- perturbing encoder parameters changes the full-memory candidate embeddings on the very next forward call; nothing is cached across the perturbation.
checks.D_chunk_equivalence_scores_losses_and_al: PASSED -- unchunked (cand_chunk_size >= N) vs. chunked streaming (cand_chunk_size << N, deliberately awkward relative to N) training on identical initial encoder/SetConditioner/UtilityHead weights produce matching smoothl1_loss/pairwise_loss (atol 1e-4) and matching gradients on every encoder, SetConditioner, and UtilityHead parameter (atol 1e-3, rtol 1e-2). Running to completion with many chunk iterations without a RuntimeError also exercises (and passes) the q_fn/m_fn fresh-recompute-per-call contract that fixes EXP-STRONG-SCORER-DIAG01's double-backward bug class, generalised here to every encoder-touching tensor.

small_N_positive_control_note: This experiment does not require a separate synthetic-known-utility positive control (unlike EXP-STRONG-SCORER-DIAG01/ASYM-SCORER01, which were testing whether a NEW scorer head could fit a target): the scorer/loss (cosine UtilityHead + R2 hybrid) is IDENTICAL to C0/R2's own, already-validated combination -- EXP-TOPTAIL-RANK01 already established that this loss/head can learn a useful top-tail signal on this exact data. The open question here is purely whether letting the ENCODER move helps or hurts; sanity checks A-D (mandatory per spec section 12) cover the new code path's correctness instead.
real_data_smoke_test: A 1-epoch, --patience 1 smoke run on the full ETTh1 train/val split was launched first and killed after ~7 minutes with no OOM/RuntimeError once GPU utilisation (97%) and steady memory (~6GB, well within budget) confirmed the streaming path was executing correctly; a targeted single-batch/single-channel timing probe (logs in this session's tool output, not a separate file) then measured 0.56-3.1s per (batch, channel) K=10-step pass depending on cand_chunk_size, used to choose cand_chunk_size=2048 and estimate full-epoch wall clock (~20-25 min) before committing to the full run.
